newsitem.title: USA: Sharp to show larger, faster screens.
newsitem.headline: Sharp to show larger, faster screens.

text.p: Sharp Electronics Corp, the U.S. unit of Osaka, Japan-based Sharp Corp, will on Monday showcase a workstation-class PC with the industry's largest high-end liquid crystal display (LCD) screen.

The 13.8 inch, active matrix 1024 by 768, XGA resolution LCD will be displayed at the Comdex industry trade show with an Intel Pentium processor at 200 megahertz processor in an 18-pound prototype being evaluated for future use in mobile engineering and other applications.
The company also said it will begin manufacturing on a trial basis the world's largest direct-viewing 40-inch color TFT LCD screen by seamlessly joining two 29-inch panels.
Sharp also said it has introduced an Internet-ready, 32-inch Widescreen television capable of accessing a family oriented information service on the Internet called Inter-TV.

The television, which is being sold in Japan for 330,000 yen, contains a built-in 28.8 kilobits per second modem anda dual function screen which enables viewers to watch television broadcasts and the Internet at the same time.
Sharp is scheduled to make 2,000 of the sets a month.
